text:
Leevi Meriläinen started this season looking like a fixed version of last year's goalie, and the last two weeks have pulled him back toward it. He is 2-7-1 and 2.33 goals below expected (goals saved above expected measures saves beyond what the shot quality predicts). Most of the damage is recent: his last five starts came in 6.25 goals below expected, while his earlier starts were on the right side of the line.

He ranks 75th of 75 goalies in our wins added, the measure of how much his saves moved his team's chances of winning. That is harsh for a goalie whose high-danger save rate (82%, 62nd percentile) is actually a hair above the league's 81%, which tells you the leaks are coming on the ordinary shots.

Context matters: last season he finished 17.93 below expected in 20 games, and our talent range puts his true save rate around .880, a bit under league average. Ottawa drafted him 71st overall in 2020, and Vancouver is still finding out what it has. We'd watch whether the routine saves come back over his next few starts, because that is the difference between a slump and a ceiling.
headline: Meriläinen's rough patch is undoing a promising start
